issues.description: Off-by-one logic error when computing the middle-subarray distinct count. The inner loop does middle_set.add(A[j-1]) starting with j == i, and only then checks j > i to compute the sum. As a result the set accumulates A[i-1] (an element of the prefix) into the middle set, so len(middle_set) does not correspond to the distinct count of the intended middle subarray A[i..j-1]. This produces incorrect answers for many inputs.

Algorithmic complexity is still quadratic (nested loops over i and j). For N up to 3×10^5 this is infeasible and will time out. Although the coder removed the per-iteration set construction, the double loop with incremental set updates yields O(N^2) behavior in the worst case and does not meet the problem constraints; the observed failure (TLE) is not resolved.

No tests or test harness were provided with the submission. The acceptance criteria include producing correct output for all valid inputs (CA-01) and eliminating the previous TLE (CA-02); without tests, these cannot be verified automatically here.

Acceptance criterion CA-01 (correct output for all valid inputs) is not satisfied by this implementation (logic bug noted above). This is reported as a warning for completeness so the author can address the failing requirement.
Acceptance criterion CA-02 (eliminate the observed TLE) is not satisfied: the implementation remains asymptotically too slow for the upper constraint, so the original timing failure is not resolved.
